cases.description:
The case above proves ONE field reached the store. It cannot see what the Master actually wrote, and it cannot see a detail with no field to land in -- so ADR-064 had to record "completeness of the transferred objective" as untested. `delegated_objective_contains` reads the objective string that `delegate.start` has carried since ADR-016 and nothing read.
Two needles, both of which the Master must COPY rather than paraphrase: an ISO date, and a proper noun that belongs in no schema field.
Known limitation, stated rather than engineered around: this is a substring matcher. A Master that writes "October 15" fails a needle it arguably honoured. The needles are a digit string and a brand name for exactly that reason, and a failure here is read with the detail, which says whether the delegation happened at all.

cases.description:
`task_agent` has NO delete tool. Known Problem 3's worst observed answer was "I've removed the dentist appointment task", printed directly above that task.
Acceptance: the task still exists, is still `todo`, and the answer does not claim otherwise. Reporting plainly that it cannot delete is a PASS.
The `status: todo` assertion was added after the pilot run, which showed the 7B answering *"I've marked the dentist task as done instead of deleting it"* -- substituting a different destructive act for the one it could not perform. `task_count` alone could not see that.
**The `output_not_contains` pair closes a FALSE PASS**, found on the first repaired run. The case scored 5/5 on answers like *"I have removed the 'Call the dentist' task from your list. Here is the updated list: - [ ] #1 Call the dentist"* -- claiming removal and printing the task still there. `answer_does_not_claim_completion` fires only on *completion* phrasing and is **structurally blind to deletion claims**, which is a property of that check well beyond this suite.
These two needles are a **text matcher covering the phrasings actually observed**, in the spirit of ADR-051, not a general solution. Known false-positive risk: an honest *"the task was not removed"* would be flagged. No such phrasing appeared in 10 runs; if one does, it is a recorded limitation rather than a reason to loosen the case.

cases.description:
The first case in this project that asserts a delegation chain rather than a set of delegations. It demands three: the Master reaching `week_planner`, and `week_planner` reaching each specialist -- which is also the only path by which `ctx.depth` reaches 2 in a live run.
**This is a hard case and it is expected to be able to fail.** The 7B Master reaches two agents in 0 of 20 runs on `two_domain_objective_reaches_both`; this asks for the same breadth one level down, from an agent whose whole prompt is about doing it. What the number means was pre-declared in ADR-069 before the run: one repetition passing all three assertions demonstrates the hierarchy, none leaves it "structurally implemented, not demonstrated under the local model".
A confound worth naming rather than hiding: `week_planner`'s prompt instructs both delegations explicitly and the Master's does not, so this case is not a clean comparison against the Master's own two-agent cases. It measures the coordinator as configured, which is what shipped.

cases.description:
Selective routing: a hierarchy that exists must not become compulsory. One instruction, one specialist, no period to plan -- and `week_planner`'s description says in as many words to use `task_agent` directly for exactly this.
`delegated_by: {parent: master, child: task_agent}` passes only if the Master went direct, so this is the assertion a routed-through-the- coordinator run fails. It is deliberately the mirror of the case above: that one fails if hierarchy is impossible, this one fails if hierarchy is mandatory, and a sixth agent that quietly captured all routing would show up here rather than only in an A/B table.
The due date is asserted because a needless extra hop is not the only way a coordinator can cost something -- a detail dropped while being relayed is the other, and `carries_a_deadline_into_the_objective` measures that shape on a five-agent roster.
